key_insight: Lifting improves mid-circuit measurement reliability by combining repetition-encoded readout signals with neural decoding and in situ calibration, reducing state-discrimination errors on noisy quantum hardware.
engineering_relevance: The framework is directly relevant for fault-tolerant quantum computing because better state discrimination makes error correction, feedback control, and measurement-driven circuits more dependable on superconducting processors.
method: Repetition-encode readout using joint in-phase and quadrature (I-Q) signals from target and auxiliary qubits.
Train a neural decoder with contextual in situ calibration so it matches the execution conditions seen during the workload.
Use theoretical analysis to show extra channels from the same joint distribution cannot worsen Bayes risk and can tighten overlap-based error bounds.
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates Lifting on three IBM processors using repeated stabilizer measurement, parity-check, and teleportation workloads.
watch_item: Performance depends on collecting and calibrating additional readout channels during execution, which may add hardware overhead and require careful workload-specific tuning.
paper_title: Lifting: Quantum State Discrimination Framework for Mid-Circuit Measurements
